seoTitle: Crucible — a native Plex client for iPhone and Apple TV
metaDescription: Crucible is an open-source, native Plex client for iPhone and Apple TV: a Resume-first Home, offline downloads, Skip Intro, Picture-in-Picture, a Liquid Glass tvOS app with native menus and a Year-in-Review dashboard.
heroHeadline: Plex, done right on iPhone and Apple TV
heroSubhead: A fast, native Plex client for iPhone and a Liquid Glass living-room app for Apple TV, both on one engine: a Resume-first Home, Skip Intro, a Year in Review of your viewing and menus that look like the system's own. Open source, and the iPhone app is built entirely on Arch Linux without ever opening Xcode.
highlights: A Resume-first Home on both: Continue Watching and Up Next lead, the artwork does the rest
Apple TV: a cinematic Home, the system player, native menus and Top Shelf
iPhone: offline downloads with a Live Activity, Skip Intro, Picture-in-Picture and background audio
Open source under GPL-3.0 — one dependency, GRDB, for the stats store

features.title: Made for the couch
features.body: On Apple TV a full-screen backdrop follows focus, the hero shows the title, details and synopsis, and rails of Continue Watching, Up Next and Recently Added sit under it. Select opens, Play/Pause plays, and a long press opens a native context menu with the card's actions. Liquid Glass controls on tvOS 26; the classic look with the same layout on older systems.

features.title: A player that respects your time
features.body: Skip Intro and Skip Credits from Plex markers — on iPhone as a button with a live progress sweep, automatic with Undo, or off; on Apple TV as native actions on the system player, with an Up Next card that counts down to the next episode. Picture-in-Picture, background audio and lock-screen controls come along on iPhone.

features.title: Take it offline
features.body: Download movies, whole seasons, or single episodes at the quality you pick — from Original down to Data Saver. A season sheet downloads all, unwatched, or the next three episodes and can keep the next ones downloaded as you watch. Downloads keep running in the background, auto-resume, and stay Wi-Fi-only unless you say otherwise, with a storage summary and one-tap cleanup of watched titles. A Live Activity tracks progress on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island — a WidgetKit extension compiled and signed entirely on Arch Linux via xtool.

features.title: Plays anything
features.body: Direct play when your device handles the file natively, automatic HLS transcoding through Plex's universal transcoder when it doesn't.

features.title: Browse the way you think
features.body: Home opens on a Resume hero, then Continue Watching, Up Next and Recently Added; on iPhone also your week in watch time. Every library has filter chips for Unwatched and In Progress, genre and sort, an A–Z scrubber, a Recently Watched rail with See All, and raw folder browsing. Search groups results by type with a Top Result. On Apple TV each movie or show library gets its own tab.

features.title: Discover more
features.body: Cast and crew, More Like This recommendations, subtitle and audio track selection, and adjustable playback speed on every title.

features.title: Know your viewing
features.body: The You tab shows your server and connection status, Watch History grouped by day, and a Year-in-Review dashboard — watch time, streaks, an activity heatmap, top shows, binges and taste from your own Plex history, on iPhone and on Apple TV. Share it as a Story or Square poster you preview first, and choose which libraries count toward Home and your stats.

features.title: Continues across devices
features.body: Watch progress syncs to your server, so Resume picks up where you left off on your phone, your TV or anywhere else you sign in. Handoff and Spotlight carry titles between your Apple devices, and the Apple TV signs in from your phone with a short code and a QR code.

features.title: Built different
features.body: Swift 6 and programmatic UIKit, with one shared engine under both apps: networking, playback, statistics and every screen's rules are shared, and the screens only render them. Liquid Glass, Light and Dark, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver throughout. The iPhone app is cross-compiled on Arch Linux and deployed over USB with no Xcode and no macOS; the Apple TV app is an Xcode project.

howItWorks.body: Authenticate with Plex over OAuth on iPhone, or with a short code and QR code from your phone on Apple TV. Crucible discovers your servers and picks the best reachable connection automatically.
Pick up with the Resume hero, filter your poster grids, or search across everything you own.
Direct play or transcode, skip the intro, send it to Picture-in-Picture, and let Up Next roll the next episode.

faq.q: Is Crucible on the App Store?
faq.a: No. Crucible is a free, open-source personal project, not an App Store release. You build the iPhone app once with xtool and sign it with your own Apple ID, about fifteen minutes with a free Apple ID, and the Apple TV app with Xcode. GitHub releases carry the changelog, not an installable app.

faq.q: Is there an Apple TV app?
faq.a: Yes, since 2.1.0. It is a separate tvOS app built for the Siri Remote on the same engine as the iPhone app: a cinematic Home, a tab for every library, search, movie, show and episode pages, the system player with Skip Intro and Skip Credits as native actions and an Up Next card, Watch History, Statistics, a Year in Review card and a Top Shelf extension. It runs on tvOS 17 or later; tvOS 26 on an Apple TV 4K (2nd generation or later) gets Liquid Glass controls, and older systems and boxes get the classic look with the same layout.

faq.q: Can I build the Apple TV app on Linux?
faq.a: No. xtool doesn't support tvOS, so the Apple TV app needs a Mac with Xcode 26 or newer and XcodeGen. The iPhone app can still be built on Linux, Windows (WSL) or a Mac.

faq.q: Do I need a Mac or Xcode to build it?
faq.a: No. Crucible is written in Swift 6 and programmatic UIKit and built with SwiftPM and xtool, which runs on Linux, Windows (WSL) and macOS and installs to an iPhone over USB. Building it on Linux without a Mac is exactly how it is made.

faq.q: How long does a free Apple ID build last?
faq.a: Seven days. After that the app stops opening until you install it again: plug the phone in and run `./scripts/install-ios.sh` once more. A paid Apple Developer account lasts a year.

faq.q: What does it need to run?
faq.a: An iPhone on iOS 17 or later, or an Apple TV on tvOS 17 or later, and a Plex Media Server you can reach. Crucible talks directly to your server, so a device away from home needs a route to it; it works well over Tailscale.

Not on your home network. To stream away from home, Plex asks for a Plex Pass on the server owner's account or a Remote Watch Pass on yours, and Skip Intro and Skip Credits rely on markers that a Plex Pass server detects. Those are Plex's rules, not Crucible's, and they can change.

faq.q: Does it support Skip Intro, PiP, and lock-screen controls?
faq.a: Yes. Skip Intro and Skip Credits come from Plex chapter markers, on iPhone and on Apple TV. On iPhone, Picture-in-Picture and background audio keep playback going and the lock screen and Control Center drive play, skip, scrub, and next episode. On Apple TV they are native actions on the system player.

faq.q: Can I download movies and shows to watch offline?
faq.a: Yes. Download movies, full seasons, or single episodes at the quality you choose — Original, High, Medium, Low, or Data Saver. Downloads run in the background and resume after interruptions, stay Wi-Fi-only unless you allow cellular, and live in a dedicated Downloads tab with a storage summary, the live queue, and one-tap cleanup of watched titles. A season sheet downloads all, unwatched, or the next three episodes, and can keep the next ones downloaded as you watch. A Live Activity shows live progress on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, and a notification fires when a download finishes while you're away. Offline playback uses the same player, so Skip Intro/Credits, resume, PiP, background audio, and lock-screen controls all work with no network.

faq.q: Can I leave a library out of Home and my statistics?
faq.a: Yes. Settings › Libraries has a switch for each library, and the Statistics screen has the same switches in a filter menu. Libraries you've hidden from Home in Plex start switched off, and at least one library always stays on.
Yes — GPL-3.0, with one third-party dependency (GRDB, for the statistics store) and pure Apple frameworks for everything else. Read the code, file an issue, or fork it on GitHub.

ctaLine: Build it, side-load it, watch everything.
pricingNote: Free and open source under GPL-3.0. The iPhone app is built on Arch Linux with xtool; the Apple TV app with Xcode.

install.title: Put it on your iPhone,
install.intro: Crucible isn't on the App Store. You build it yourself: the iPhone app once with xtool, signed with your own Apple ID, over USB (a free Apple ID is enough); the Apple TV app with Xcode on a Mac. You need an iPhone on iOS 17 or later, a cable, and a Mac, a Linux PC, or Windows with WSL.

steps.title: Install xtool
steps.body: xtool builds and installs iOS apps without Xcode's interface. On a Mac, install Xcode 26 or newer from the App Store, open it once, then install xtool.
steps.note: On Linux or Windows (WSL) you install Swift 6.4, usbmuxd, and Xcode's `.xip` from Apple instead; the step-by-step guide below lists each command.

steps.title: Sign in to Apple
steps.body: Pick `1: Password` to use any Apple ID, a free one included, then enter the two-factor code. Your credentials go only to Apple. On Linux and Windows it also asks for the path to the `.xip`.

steps.title: Build it and put it on your phone
steps.body: Plug the phone in, unlock it and tap Trust. The script checks your setup, builds Crucible in release mode and installs it. The first build takes several minutes. If it asks for Developer Mode, turn it on in Settings > Privacy & Security, restart the phone and run the script again.

steps.title: Trust it and open it
steps.body: On the phone: Settings > General > VPN & Device Management > your Apple ID > Trust, then open Crucible and sign in with Plex. A free Apple ID's build stops opening after 7 days; run the script again to renew it.

steps.title: Apple TV, optional
steps.body: The Apple TV app is an Xcode project, because xtool doesn't support tvOS. It needs a Mac with Xcode 26 or newer and XcodeGen. Generate the project, open it, choose your signing team and run it on your paired Apple TV; the README and `tv/README.md` cover the details.
code: cd Crucible/tv && xcodegen generate && open CrucibleTV.xcodeproj
steps.note: The Top Shelf extension needs the App Group capability, so it only shows up when your signing setup provides it. tvOS 17 or later; Liquid Glass needs tvOS 26 on an Apple TV 4K (2nd generation) or later.
